Theme

School & learning

intransitive adjective

also intransitive verb, intransitive verbs

classical

Gell. 1.7.15 (Lewis & Short s.v. neuter)
Traupman 227

neuter, neutra, neutrum

declension

intransitive, neither active nor passive (of verbs)

verba neutra are verbs that are neither active nor passive, such as sedeō, stō, cubō (Traupman 228); Lewis & Short also cites Cic. Or. 155 for the usage.

Other words

  • intrānsitīvus, intrānsitīva, intrānsitīvum — intransitive

    declension · also used · late Latin · Prisc. p. 982 P. (Lewis & Short); Traupman 247; Traupman 334

    A term of the later grammarians; the opposite is trānsitīvus.

  • neutrālis, neutrāle — intransitive (of verbs)

    declension · also used · modern · Traupman 227, 228, 244

    Traupman’s verbum neutrāle. Lewis & Short gives neutrālis only of the neuter gender (Quintilian); we have found no ancient instance of it for verbs.

Examples

  • Dā exempla verbī neutrālis. — Sedeō, stō, cubō.

    Give some examples of an intransitive verb. — I sit, I stand, I lie.Traupman 228

See also transitive, neuter, voice, grammar.
